Hi all —

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa. Attaching a concise architecture note (redwood-dedicated-arch.pdf) with recommended defaults and then specifics for your 350 QPS target. High-level points below — see the doc for diagrams and numbers:

1) SDK setup & auth
- Use Redwood SDK with API keys scoped to the dedicated deployment. For Private/VPC we'll exchange a short-lived onboarding key and provision a tenant-scoped API key for your service accounts.
- Recommended flow: server-side token exchange -> short-lived SDK token (rotate daily).

2) Routing (prod vs dev)
- Route by API key prefix/environments. We recommend two logical routes: prod route pinned to the dedicated capacity (SLA-backed), dev route to hosted capacity to avoid consuming reserved units.
- Canary policy: route 5-10% for new model variants for 48 hrs, automatic fallback if latency/err rate spike.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We support streaming structured output + function/tool calling. For tool calls, include a lightweight schema in the call metadata. Server-side SDK will validate and surface partial responses for long-running tools.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Store embeddings in your vector DB (we recommend Pinecone/FAISS as discussed). Our recommender: compute in-batch reranks server-side (inference + small MLP) to minimize round trips.
- For live rerank bursts, ensure concurrency headroom (see queues below).

5) Autoscaling, throughput sizing, concurrency, and queues (summary)
- Baseline: for 350 QPS at seq_len 512 and standard LLM profile, we recommend initial pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved). This assumes steady batching with continuous batching enabled.
- Concurrency per GPU: target 8 concurrent inflight requests (depends on model footprint).
- Queue sizing: two-level queueing — per-route short queue (max 100 requests) + global overflow queue for bursts (policy: drop / 429 after 30s).
- Autoscaling policy: scale by 20% increments based on sustained 5-min CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth thresholds; warm-up instances immediately for predicted business-hour bursts via scheduled scaling (cron).

I've attached the architecture doc and a simple sizing workbook. Dev, feel free to add any tuning specifics.

Cheers,
Aditya
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-arch.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); acme-mtp-sizing.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

2) For the two-level queueing scheme: what happens to long-running rerank requests that exceed the per-route queue but are still important (we can't drop them)?
3) For auth: our security team prefers short-lived mTLS certs instead of API keys. Is that supported for Dedicated/Private?

We can share a sampled hour of traffic from last week (CloudWatch CSV) — attaching it now. Would like to keep the follow-up tech session to 45 minutes if possible.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: integration & autoscaling follow-up

Thanks Emily — quick answers below:

1) Tokens/sec per GPU: we use a conservative baseline of ~2500 tokens/sec for a 512-seq generation workload on an A100-equivalent with continuous batching. That maps to ~312.5 requests/sec if average response is 8 tokens — but for longer responses or heavy sampling your effective RPS is lower. The "8 GPUs" number assumes average of ~4-6 tokens generation per request; we'll refine after we run your sample traffic through our benchmark harness.

2) Long-running reranks: we support a "priority queue" option for critical rerank jobs that routes to a reserved worker pool (pre-warmed nodes). For those, we recommend a separate route + API key so they don't contend with regular requests. Fallback policy: if reserved pool exhausted, requests can queue in global overflow but are marked as "best-effort" and we surface progress via the SDK callbacks.

3) mTLS support: yes — Dedicated/Private supports mutual TLS for service-to-service auth. We'll work with your security team on cert rotation cadence (we recommend 7-14 day short-lived certs for high-security tenants).

Next steps:
- If you can upload the sample CloudWatch CSV to the Drive link I shared, I'll run a workload profile and get back with a refined GPU count + concrete p95 latency estimates by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: can we lock Wed 11:00-11:45 PT for the tech session?

Thanks,
